title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S is a scheme in characteristic 0 and X/S is presumably a smooth relative curve, since J/J^2 is required to be invertible. The page is the formal-geometric core of a treatment of projective connections (projective structures) on X/S, in the service of uniformisation.

Given data. Let P = lim P_n be a complete adic O_X-algebra, augmented to O_X, with augmentation ideal J. Assume J/J^2 = ω is invertible, so P is locally O_X[[t]]. P carries a connection C relative to S, i.e. a Grothendieck-type connection/stratification on the formal-disc bundle Spf P → X. C respects the algebra structure but need not respect the augmentation. The prototype is the completed principal-parts algebra P^∞_{X/S}, i.e. O_{X×X} completed along the diagonal, with its canonical connection. The hypothesis on the struck line is a transversality (Kodaira–Spencer type) condition: the map ω = J/J^2 → Ω^1_{X/S} induced by C, via C: Ĵ → P ⊗ Ω^1 reduced mod J, is an isomorphism. On a relative curve the connection is automatically integrable.

Problem. Find triples (P, σ, c) together with an isomorphism of augmented algebras u: Ŝ ≅ P such that u(ĉ) = C. Here:
- P is a P^1-bundle over X (the text says 'fibré en droites', surely meaning a projective-line bundle).
- σ is a section of P.
- c is a connection on P not required to preserve σ.
- Ŝ = O of the formal completion of P along σ.
- ĉ is the connection induced by c on Ŝ.
In modern terms: a PGL_2-oper / projective connection, presented as a P^1-bundle with a marked section and a connection transversal to it.

Claims.
(a) An isomorphism u_2 at order 2, i.e. modulo the cube of the ideal, already determines (P, σ) up to unique isomorphism. Through J/J^3 it gives an extension 0 → Ω → E → O → 0 with Ω = J/J^2, and P = P(E) with σ given by the quotient (or sub) line.
(b) Fix (P, σ). Every order-3 isomorphism Ŝ/Ĵ^4 → P/J^4 extending u_2 extends uniquely to a full isomorphism û such that û^{-1}(C) has the form ĉ for a connection c on P.

Consequence (next page). The category of solutions is rigid. Solutions up to isomorphism correspond bijectively to order-3 lifts of u_2. These lifts form a pseudo-torsor under Γ(X, Ω^{⊗2}). So projective structures compatible with the given transversal formal-disc crystal form a torsor under quadratic differentials: the classical Schwarzian/torsor statement. The previous page phrases the same thing group-theoretically. G is the group of automorphisms of Ŝ that are the identity to order 2, acting on Conn(Ŝ). Solutions correspond to G-orbits meeting the set of connections of the form ĉ, with stabiliser and coset analysis (h ĉ = ĉ ⇒ h = 1).
errors: 'fibrés en droites P' must mean P^1-bundles (fibrés en droites projectives) with a section, not line bundles; the transcription/notation is ambiguous.
The formula 'E = Ω ⊗ (J/J^3)' as transcribed is not right. E (or its dual) should come from J/J^3 or (P/J^3)^∨ via 0→Ω→E→O→0; likely a transcription garble.

The transversality hypothesis is written then heavily struck; the exact condition (J/J^2 → Ω^1_{X/S} iso induced by C) must be assumed for (b) to hold. Without it, uniqueness/existence of the extension fails.

Part (b) is stated as existence and uniqueness of the extension. The proof (inductive order-by-order solving, using char 0 and invertibility of the Kodaira–Spencer map) is not given on this page. The phrase 'pseudo-torseur' on the next page correctly hedges existence.

ideas.what: Encoding a projective structure on a curve as a P^1-bundle with section and a connection transversal to the section, via the formal completion along the section compared with a formal-disc bundle carrying a flat connection
ideas.modern_name: PGL_2-opers (Beilinson–Drinfeld); projective connections à la Gunning/Deligne; formal geometry (Gelfand–Kazhdan)

ideas.what: Order-2 jet of the identification determines the extension 0→Ω→E→O→0, hence (P,σ), up to unique isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Jet/Atiyah-type extension defining the oper bundle (rank-2 bundle J^1 of Ω^{-1/2}-type)

ideas.what: Order-3 data determines a unique compatible full isomorphism; solutions form a pseudo-torsor under Γ(X, Ω^{⊗2}); the solution category is rigid
ideas.modern_name: Projective structures form a torsor under quadratic differentials (Schwarzian derivative); opers are rigid (no automorphisms)

ideas.what: Relative, characteristic-0, arbitrary-base-S formulation via Grothendieck connections on complete augmented adic algebras
ideas.modern_name: Crystals of formal discs / Harish-Chandra (Aut O) torsors over the de Rham stack

missed.claim: Grothendieck developed, apparently independently and at an unknown date, a formal-geometric (crystalline) characterisation of projective structures on relative curves over an arbitrary char-0 base. The characterisation is: a transversal flat connection on a formal-disc bundle, matched to the completion of a P^1-bundle along a section. This is essentially the Beilinson–Drinfeld oper / Aut O-torsor viewpoint.
missed.quote: munis d'une connexion c (non respectant pas la section marquée σ) ... et leurs iso d'algèbres augm. Ŝ ↔ P ... tel que u(ĉ) = C
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, this may predate the oper formalism. Mathematically, the content (torsor under quadratic differentials, rigidity) is now standard, so it matters mainly for attribution once the notes are dated.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean formal-geometry / Grothendieck-connection treatment of projective connections anticipating the oper and Aut O-torsor viewpoint. The results themselves (order-2 determines the bundle, order-3 lifts form a torsor under quadratic differentials, rigidity) are well known, so there is little new mathematics; interest is mainly historical and depends on the undated manuscript.
transcription_corrections: 'une 𝓕 connexion C' is probably just 'une connexion C' (the symbol is a struck or decorated letter).
'fibrés en droites P' is likely 'fibrés en droites projectives P' (P^1-bundles).
'σ_2' in (a) is uncertain; reads more like 'i.e. σ,' followed by 'à iso unique près'.
'E = Ω ⊗ (J/J^3)' is uncertain; the image suggests 'E = Ω^∨ ⊗ (J/J^3)' or similar; it defines the extension 0→Ω→E→O→0.
The struck line under the hypotheses reads roughly 'la [condition] J/J^2 = ω → Ω^1_{X/S}' (Kodaira–Spencer-type iso induced by C).
'(Algébriquement' is more likely '(Algébrique,' or 'Algébrique formelle'; uncertain.
